newsitem.title: Belgium: EU confirms proposed ban on ostrich imports.
newsitem.headline: EU confirms proposed ban on ostrich imports.

text.p: The European Union's standing veterinary committee has proposed a ban on the import of ostrich meat and live ostriches from South Africa after an outbreak of Congo fever, a Commission spokesman said on Thursday.
Spokesman Gerry Kiely said the commission would examine the imports of ostrich meat from other African countries, but did not envisage a ban on imports from Britain.
Ostrich meat has gained in popularity in Europe in recent years due in part to health fears about beef possibly infected with "mad cow disease".

In Pretoria earlier, the South African Health Department said the ban had been proposed as a precautionary measure, "due to the uncertainty about the safty of ostrich meat for human consumption in the event of an outbreak of Congo fever".
Up to 17 people working at an ostrich abattoir are feared to have contracted the tick-borne fever. One of them has died.

Congo-Crimean haemorrhagic fever is an infectious disease that, like the more notorious viral disease Ebola, causes body organs to degenerate with massive internal and some external bleeding. About 30 percent of Congo fever cases are fatal.
